runtime_flows.name: CLI startup flow
steps: Process invokes the console script `minisvc`, which resolves to minisvc.cli:main via pyproject.toml.
load_settings resolves MINISVC_DB or falls back to orders.sqlite and parses MINISVC_READONLY into Settings.readonly.
main calls OrderRepository.init_schema(), which creates the SQLite orders table if missing.
main prints `minisvc ready at <database_path>` and exits with status code 0.

runtime_flows.name: HTTP create-order flow
steps: The embedding web app calls minisvc.api.routes:register_routes(app, repo).
register_routes wires POST /orders to minisvc.api.handlers:create_order through a lambda that closes over repo.
A POST payload reaches create_order(payload, repo).
create_order reads payload["order_id"], payload["customer"], and payload["total_cents"], coercing total_cents to int.
create_order instantiates minisvc.models:Order from those values.
create_order calls OrderRepository.save(order), which inserts the row into the SQLite orders table using sqlite3.
create_order calls minisvc.audit:order_event(order, "created") to build an in-memory event dict.
create_order returns {status: "created", order_id: ..., event: ...}; there is no retry loop, readonly gate, or persisted audit write.
